title: Does learning raise social actions by weakening locomotion?
question: In Experiment I, every input weight fell over a lifetime and locomotion weights fell the most, even when credit went only to the executed action. Action choice is a spike-count competition, so weaker locomotion could let every social action win more often. If locomotion inputs are frozen and only social inputs may learn, does the learning-induced rise in attacking, signalling and sharing shrink?
background: Experiment I: under learning, drift (learned/innate - 1) was -0.032 for locomotion and -0.004 to -0.011 for social actions. Crediting only the executed action removed none of the attack rise and about half of the signalling rise. Intervention: frozen_inputs = [left, forward, right] keeps locomotion input weights at their innate values while social inputs keep learning. Caveat: this also removes all lifetime learning of foraging. Seeds 300-307 have never been run.

hypotheses.statement: Freezing locomotion inputs lowers the attack rate
Freezing locomotion inputs lowers sharing given a neighbour in reach
With locomotion frozen, learning no longer raises the attack rate above no-learning
Manipulation check: social inputs drift up relative to locomotion under learn_all (replicates I's H18b)
